_in_flight: IN FLIGHT, not docked - the opposite of scenario 019, and for a measured reason: the HUD is drawn over the 3-D view only. While docked the screen is a station GUI and all three 'modes' render the same picture, so the between-mode differential this scenario rests on would measure nothing. `in_flight` and the guiScreen at every capture are recorded as evidence rather than assumed.
_pose: The `ref` pose of tests/golden/frame_capture.py: the origin of the save's system frame, identity orientation, looking at the planet and sun - the only large stable features an emptied system has. The 3-D stimulus is held CONSTANT across all three modes; only the overlay changes. Re-applied and read back BEFORE EVERY capture, because a drifting camera is indistinguishable from a HUD difference.
_hud_modes: THE SUBJECT. Three modes over two stock plists: hud.plist (the default, PlayerEntity.m:1982 and :4515 both fall back to it), hud-small.plist (the other stock HUD shipped in Resources/Config), and hud.plist with hudHidden true - the overlay suppressed entirely. The hidden mode deliberately keeps hud.plist loaded so the ONLY difference between it and the primary mode is whether the overlay is DRAWN; pointing it at hud-small.plist would confound two changes in one arm.
_primary_mode: Which mode's frame becomes frame.grid and frame.png, named explicitly rather than taken as 'the first entry' - a positional rule silently re-blesses a different frame the day someone reorders the list. It is also the mode captured a SECOND time in the same run to give the within-mode witness.
_unknown_hud_plist: THE ENGINE REFUSAL. -switchHudTo: (PlayerEntity.m:4537-4542) looks the name up with dictionaryFromFilesNamed: and, when that yields nil, logs PlayerEntity.switchHudTo.failed and returns NO WITHOUT TOUCHING the HUD. So writing this name must leave player.ship.hud reading the previous one. A permissive model that stores whatever string it is handed reports this name back instead - which is why the refusal is POSITIVE evidence where 'no ERROR lines' is not (bead oo-het's exit-87 corpse carried zero ERROR lines).
_within_mode_tolerance: MEASURED BY THIS SCENARIO, not inherited. The catalogue marks 020 buildable-pending-own-calibration because the shared 0.004377 in tests/golden/calibration.json was derived by bead oo-ae9 from 3-D SCENE changes and says nothing about whether a HUD OVERLAY clears the bar. `hud_render_modes.py --calibrate 4` measured both populations on this host, 12 captures each from ITS OWN game process (129.6 s), with the per-capture clear-to-fixed-point in place so no ambient ship could inflate the within-mode side: within-mode 18 pairs at 0.001592..0.002073, between-mode 48 pairs at 0.011000..0.022383. NON-OVERLAPPING with a 5.31x gap, and the threshold is the geometric mean of the worst within and the best between - frame_hash.derive_tolerance's own rule, which places it at an equal MULTIPLICATIVE margin (2.30x) from each population. The raw populations are stored in provenance.json.calibration.
_min_separation_ratio: A FLOOR ON THE MARGIN ITSELF, so a run cannot pass by shrinking the stimulus until the modes are barely distinguishable. Measured separation between the two populations was 5.31x (best between 0.011000 / worst within 0.002073), and the weakest of 10 stability runs still separated by 5.83x; the floor is set at 2.0x - comfortably under what was measured, comfortably above 1.0x (which would accept populations that merely fail to overlap). A run that drops under it is a finding to investigate, never a reason to lower this number.
_frame_liveness_floor: The one frame property a dead run cannot fake: the luminance SPREAD (max-min)/255 of the 64x64 grid. An empty or never-drawn render is ~0.0. Measured across every calibration capture of this scenario at 0.7176..0.7294, so the floor of 0.2 sits at 0.28x the weakest observed value - a vacuity guard, not a tight assertion, because a tight one would gate the renderer rather than the HUD.
_min_png_bytes: A black frame compresses to ~5 KB; real captures of this scene on this 960x720 surface measured 224301..243085 bytes across the calibration sweep. 50000 is the catalogue's own floor and sits far above the black-frame case and far below every real one.
_repopulator_handlers: oolite-populator.js's repopulate handler. Its station picker `_tradeStation` tests hasNPCTraffic inside its loop but ENDS WITH an unconditional `return system.mainStation`, so switching the flag off does not stop it launching. The name is pinned here so an upstream rename becomes a red rather than a silent no-op. This scenario FLIES, so ambient traffic drifting into frame between two captures would be a real difference and would inflate the within-mode population - suppression is load-bearing here in a way it is not for a docked scenario.
